fr.R: Saül, les frères de David et toute l’armée d’Israël étaient dans la vallée du Térébinthe pour se battre contre les Philistins.

vi.L: Sau-lơ, họ và mọi người Y-sơ-ra-ên [đang ở] trong thung lũng Ê-la, đánh nhau với người Phi-li-tin.
vi.B: Sau-lơ cùng các anh của Đa-vít và toàn quân Y-sơ-ra-ên đang ở trong thung lũng Ê-la, giao chiến với người Phi-li-tin.
vi.R: Sau-lơ, các anh của Đa-vít và toàn thể quân đội Y-sơ-ra-ên đang ở trong thung lũng Ê-la, chiến đấu chống lại người Phi-li-tin.

decisions.choice: the narrator's words
decisions.reason: This verse could be the end of Jesse's words, telling David where to find his brothers, or the narrator's note. It is read here as the narrator's, since Jesse has finished his instructions.

decisions.choice: fighting: at war, though no battle had yet been fought
decisions.reason: The word describes the state of war: the armies were drawn up against each other (verses 2-3, 16), but no battle was fought until David's victory.

decisions.choice: the brothers; David's brothers
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who "they" are.

source.text: וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֨ם דָּוִ֜ד בַּבֹּ֗קֶר וַיִּטֹּ֤שׁ אֶת־הַצֹּאן֙ עַל־שֹׁמֵ֔ר וַיִּשָּׂ֣א וַיֵּ֔לֶךְ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוָּ֖הוּ יִשָׁ֑י וַיָּבֹא֙ הַמַּעְגָּ֔לָה וְהַחַ֗יִל הַיֹּצֵא֙ אֶל־הַמַּ֣עֲרָכָ֔ה וְהֵרֵ֖עוּ בַּמִּלְחָמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And rose early David in the morning and left the flock with a keeper, and lifted up and went, as had commanded him Jesse; and he came to the encampment, and the army [was] going out to the battle line, and they shouted [the] war cry for battle.

en.L: And David rose early in the morning and left the flock with a keeper, and he loaded up and went as Jesse had commanded him; and he came to the encampment as the army was going out to the battle line, and they were shouting the war cry for battle.
en.B: David got up early in the morning, left the sheep with someone to watch them, loaded up the food, and set out as Jesse had told him. He reached the camp just as the army was going out to its battle positions, shouting the war cry.
en.R: So David got up early the next morning. He left the sheep with someone to watch them, packed up the food, and went, just as his father Jesse had told him. He reached the army camp just as the soldiers were marching out to their battle positions, shouting their battle cry.

es.L: Y se levantó David de madrugada, y dejó el rebaño con un guarda, y cargó y fue, como le había mandado Isaí; y llegó al cerco del campamento cuando el ejército salía a la línea de batalla, y lanzaban el grito de guerra para la batalla.
es.B: David se levantó temprano por la mañana, dejó las ovejas con alguien que las cuidara, cargó la comida y se puso en camino, como Isaí le había mandado. Llegó al campamento justo cuando el ejército salía a sus posiciones de combate lanzando el grito de guerra.
es.R: Así que David se levantó temprano a la mañana siguiente. Dejó las ovejas con alguien que las cuidara, preparó la comida y se fue, como le había dicho su padre Isaí. Llegó al campamento del ejército justo cuando los soldados salían a sus posiciones de combate, gritando su grito de guerra.

fr.L: Et David se leva tôt le matin et laissa le troupeau à un gardien, et il chargea et partit, comme Jessé le lui avait ordonné ; et il arriva au campement, alors que l’armée sortait vers la ligne de bataille, et ils poussaient le cri de guerre pour la bataille.
fr.B: David se leva de bon matin, confia les moutons à un gardien, chargea les vivres et partit, comme Jessé le lui avait ordonné. Il arriva au camp au moment où l’armée sortait pour prendre ses positions de combat en poussant le cri de guerre.
fr.R: David s’est donc levé tôt le lendemain matin. Il a laissé les moutons à quelqu’un pour les garder, il a pris la nourriture et il est parti, comme son père Jessé le lui avait dit. Il est arrivé au camp de l’armée juste au moment où les soldats partaient prendre leurs positions de combat en poussant leur cri de guerre.

vi.L: Đa-vít dậy sớm vào buổi sáng, để bầy chiên lại cho một người giữ, rồi chất đồ lên và đi như Gie-sê đã dặn cậu. Cậu đến vòng trại quân đúng lúc quân đội đang tiến ra trận tuyến và hò hét tiếng hô xung trận.
vi.B: Sáng hôm sau, Đa-vít dậy sớm, để bầy chiên lại cho một người trông coi, mang đồ ăn và lên đường như lời Gie-sê dặn. Cậu đến trại quân vừa lúc quân đội đang tiến ra vị trí chiến đấu, hô vang tiếng xung trận.
vi.R: Vậy sáng hôm sau, Đa-vít dậy sớm. Cậu để bầy chiên lại cho một người trông coi, gói ghém đồ ăn và lên đường, đúng như cha cậu là Gie-sê đã dặn. Cậu đến trại quân vừa lúc quân lính đang tiến ra vị trí chiến đấu, hô vang tiếng xung trận.

decisions.choice: the encampment: the ring of the camp
decisions.reason: The word means a circle or track. It probably names the camp's outer ring, perhaps a circle of carts or a barricade (26:5, 7).

decisions.choice: lifted up: loaded the supplies
decisions.reason: The verb "lift" here means to load and carry the food of verses 17-18.

decisions.choice: shouted the war cry: the loud shout raised before battle
decisions.reason: This is the shout an army gave as it went into battle (Joshua 6:5, 20; and 4:5 in this book).

decisions.choice: his father Jesse
decisions.reason: Readable reminds the reader who Jesse is.

source.text: וַתַּעֲרֹ֤ךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וּפְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים מַעֲרָכָ֖ה לִקְרַ֥את מַעֲרָכָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And drew up Israel and [the] Philistines battle line to meet battle line.

en.L: And Israel and the Philistines drew up battle line to meet battle line.
en.B: Israel and the Philistines were drawn up, battle line facing battle line.
en.R: The Israelites and the Philistines lined up their armies facing each other.

es.L: Y se ordenaron Israel y los filisteos, línea de batalla frente a línea de batalla.
es.B: Israel y los filisteos estaban formados, línea de batalla frente a línea de batalla.
es.R: Los israelitas y los filisteos pusieron sus ejércitos en orden, uno frente al otro.

fr.L: Et Israël et les Philistins se rangèrent, ligne de bataille contre ligne de bataille.
fr.B: Israël et les Philistins se rangèrent en bataille, ligne contre ligne.
fr.R: Les Israélites et les Philistins ont placé leurs armées face à face.

vi.L: Y-sơ-ra-ên và người Phi-li-tin dàn trận, trận tuyến đối diện trận tuyến.
vi.B: Y-sơ-ra-ên và người Phi-li-tin dàn quân, trận tuyến đối mặt với trận tuyến.
vi.R: Quân Y-sơ-ra-ên và quân Phi-li-tin dàn quân đối mặt nhau.

decisions.choice: battle line to meet battle line: the two armies face to face
decisions.reason: The repeated word pictures two ranks facing each other across the valley (verse 3).

decisions.choice: lined up their armies facing each other
decisions.reason: Readable says the picture plainly.

source.text: וַיִּטֹּשׁ֩ דָּוִ֨ד אֶת־הַכֵּלִ֜ים מֵעָלָ֗יו עַל־יַד֙ שׁוֹמֵ֣ר הַכֵּלִ֔ים וַיָּ֖רָץ הַמַּעֲרָכָ֑ה וַיָּבֹ֕א וַיִּשְׁאַ֥ל לְאֶחָ֖יו לְשָׁלֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: And left David the baggage from upon him in [the] hand of the keeper of the baggage, and ran [to] the battle line and came and asked his brothers for welfare.

en.L: And David left the baggage from on him in the hand of the keeper of the baggage, and he ran [to] the battle line and came and asked his brothers about [their] welfare.
en.B: David left his load with the keeper of the supplies, ran to the battle line, and went to ask his brothers how they were.
en.R: David left the food with the man who was guarding the supplies. Then he ran to the battle line to greet his brothers and ask how they were.

es.L: Y dejó David el equipaje de encima de él en mano del guarda del equipaje, y corrió [a] la línea de batalla, y llegó y preguntó a sus hermanos por [su] bienestar.
es.B: David dejó su carga con el encargado de las provisiones, corrió a la línea de batalla y fue a preguntar a sus hermanos cómo estaban.
es.R: David dejó la comida con el hombre que cuidaba las provisiones. Luego corrió a la línea de batalla para saludar a sus hermanos y preguntarles cómo estaban.

fr.L: Et David laissa les bagages de dessus lui entre les mains du gardien des bagages, et il courut [vers] la ligne de bataille, et il vint demander à ses frères [comment allait leur] paix.
fr.B: David laissa son chargement au gardien des bagages, courut vers la ligne de bataille et alla demander à ses frères comment ils allaient.
fr.R: David a laissé la nourriture à l’homme qui gardait les provisions. Puis il a couru vers la ligne de bataille pour saluer ses frères et leur demander comment ils allaient.

vi.L: Đa-vít để đồ đạc trên mình lại trong tay người giữ đồ đạc, rồi chạy [đến] trận tuyến, đến hỏi thăm các anh mình có bình an không.
vi.B: Đa-vít gửi đồ đạc cho người coi giữ hành lý, rồi chạy ra trận tuyến và đến hỏi thăm sức khỏe các anh mình.
vi.R: Đa-vít để đồ ăn lại cho người canh giữ hành lý. Rồi cậu chạy ra trận tuyến để chào các anh và hỏi thăm họ.

decisions.choice: the baggage: the things he carried
decisions.reason: The word means gear or things in general; here it is the food and supplies of verses 17-18. The army kept a guard over its baggage (25:13; 30:24).

decisions.choice: asked his brothers about their welfare: greeted them
decisions.reason: To ask about someone's welfare (shalom) was the usual greeting, and it was also what Jesse sent David to do (verse 18).

source.text: וְה֣וּא׀מְדַבֵּ֣ר עִמָּ֗ם וְהִנֵּ֣ה אִ֣ישׁ הַבֵּנַ֡יִם עוֹלֶ֞ה גָּלְיָת֩ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֨י שְׁמ֤וֹ מִגַּת֙ מִמַּעַרְכ֣וֹתפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וַיְדַבֵּ֖ר כַּדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיִּשְׁמַ֖ע דָּוִֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And he [was] speaking with them, and look, the man of the in-between coming up, Goliath the Philistine [was] his name, from Gath, from the battle lines of [the] Philistines, and he spoke according to these words, and David heard.

en.L: And he was speaking with them, and look, the man of the [space] between was coming up, Goliath the Philistine [was] his name, from Gath, out of the ranks of the Philistines; and he spoke the same words, and David heard.
en.B: While he was talking with them, the champion, the Philistine from Gath named Goliath, came up out of the Philistine ranks and spoke the same words as before, and David heard them.
en.R: While David was talking with them, Goliath, the Philistine champion from Gath, came out from the Philistine army. He shouted the same challenge as before, and David heard it.

es.L: Y mientras él hablaba con ellos, he aquí que el hombre de en medio subía, Goliat el filisteo [era] su nombre, de Gat, de las filas de los filisteos; y habló conforme a estas palabras, y David [lo] oyó.
es.B: Mientras hablaba con ellos, el campeón, el filisteo de Gat llamado Goliat, salió de las filas filisteas y dijo las mismas palabras de antes, y David las oyó.
es.R: Mientras David hablaba con ellos, Goliat, el campeón filisteo de Gat, salió del ejército filisteo. Gritó el mismo desafío de antes, y David lo oyó.

fr.L: Et il parlait avec eux, et voici, l’homme de l’entre-deux montait, son nom [était] Goliath le Philistin, de Gath, du milieu des rangs des Philistins ; et il parla selon ces paroles, et David entendit.
fr.B: Pendant qu’il leur parlait, le champion, le Philistin de Gath nommé Goliath, s’avança hors des rangs des Philistins et répéta les mêmes paroles, et David les entendit.
fr.R: Pendant que David parlait avec eux, Goliath, le champion philistin de Gath, est sorti de l’armée des Philistins. Il a crié le même défi qu’avant, et David l’a entendu.

vi.L: Khi cậu đang nói chuyện với họ, kìa, người của khoảng [đất] ở giữa đang đi lên, tên [là] Gô-li-át, người Phi-li-tin từ Gát, từ hàng ngũ quân Phi-li-tin; hắn nói đúng những lời như trước, và Đa-vít nghe.
vi.B: Trong lúc cậu đang nói chuyện với họ, thì tay đấu thủ, người Phi-li-tin ở Gát tên là Gô-li-át, từ hàng ngũ quân Phi-li-tin bước lên và nói lại những lời như trước. Đa-vít nghe thấy.
vi.R: Trong lúc Đa-vít đang nói chuyện với các anh, Gô-li-át, đấu thủ người Phi-li-tin từ Gát, từ đạo quân Phi-li-tin bước ra. Hắn lại hét lên lời thách thức như trước, và Đa-vít nghe thấy.

decisions.choice: out of the ranks of the Philistines
decisions.reason: The letters written in the text spell a word meaning "caves", but the tradition of reading marks them to be read "battle lines", the word used throughout the chapter. The text followed here reads "battle lines".

decisions.choice: according to these words: the same challenge as before
decisions.reason: Goliath repeats the words of verses 8-10, and now David hears them.

decisions.choice: look: the story turns to what David sees
decisions.reason: The word draws attention to a sudden event, seen as if through the eyes of the person in the story.

decisions.choice: while ... came up (Balanced); left out (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable let the sentence carry the surprise rather than use an old-fashioned word for "look".

source.text: וְכֹל֙ אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בִּרְאוֹתָ֖ם אֶת־הָאִ֑ישׁ וַיָּנֻ֨סוּ֙ מִפָּנָ֔יו וַיִּֽירְא֖וּ מְאֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And every man of Israel, when they saw the man, fled from before him and were afraid greatly.

en.L: And all the men of Israel, when they saw the man, fled from him and were greatly afraid.
en.B: Whenever the men of Israel saw the man, they all ran from him in great fear.
en.R: When the Israelite soldiers saw Goliath, they all ran away from him, terrified.

es.L: Y todos los hombres de Israel, cuando vieron al hombre, huyeron de delante de él y tuvieron mucho miedo.
es.B: Cada vez que los hombres de Israel veían a aquel hombre, todos huían de él llenos de miedo.
es.R: Cuando los soldados israelitas vieron a Goliat, todos huyeron de él aterrados.

fr.L: Et tous les hommes d’Israël, quand ils virent l’homme, s’enfuirent devant lui et eurent très peur.
fr.B: Chaque fois que les hommes d’Israël voyaient cet homme, ils s’enfuyaient tous devant lui, pris de terreur.
fr.R: Quand les soldats israélites ont vu Goliath, ils se sont tous enfuis devant lui, terrifiés.

vi.L: Mọi người Y-sơ-ra-ên, khi thấy người ấy, đều chạy trốn khỏi hắn và rất sợ hãi.
vi.B: Mỗi lần quân Y-sơ-ra-ên thấy người ấy, họ đều bỏ chạy trước mặt hắn, vô cùng sợ hãi.
vi.R: Khi quân lính Y-sơ-ra-ên thấy Gô-li-át, họ đều bỏ chạy vì quá kinh hãi.

decisions.choice: were greatly afraid: as in verse 11
decisions.reason: The same words were used of Saul and all Israel in verse 11. David's response in verses 26 and 32 stands against the fear of the whole army.

decisions.choice: fled from before him: drew back from where he was
decisions.reason: The phrase means to flee from someone's presence. The soldiers fell back each time he came near.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר׀אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הַרְּאִיתֶם֙ הָאִ֤ישׁ הָֽעֹלֶה֙ הַזֶּ֔ה כִּ֛י לְחָרֵ֥ף אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עֹלֶ֑ה וְֽ֠הָיָה הָאִ֨ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־יַכֶּ֜נּוּ יַעְשְׁרֶ֥נּוּ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ׀עֹ֣שֶׁר גָּד֗וֹל וְאֶת־בִּתּוֹ֙ יִתֶּן־ל֔וֹ וְאֵת֙ בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֔יו יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה חָפְשִׁ֖י בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And said [the] man of Israel, Have you seen this man who comes up? For to defy Israel he comes up. And it will be, the man who strikes him down, the king will make him rich [with] great riches, and his daughter he will give to him, and the house of his father he will make free in Israel.

en.L: And the men of Israel said, "Have you seen this man who is coming up? Surely he comes up to defy Israel. And the man who strikes him down, the king will make him rich with great riches, and he will give him his daughter, and he will make his father's house free in Israel."
en.B: The men of Israel were saying, "Have you seen this man coming up? He comes up to defy Israel! The king will give great wealth to the man who kills him. He will give him his daughter as well, and he will make his father's family free in Israel."
en.R: The Israelite soldiers were saying to one another, "Do you see this man? He keeps coming out to insult Israel. The king will make the man who kills him very rich. He will also let that man marry his daughter, and his father's family will not have to pay taxes or work for the king anymore."

es.L: Y dijeron los hombres de Israel: «¿{{plural_you:Han visto|Habéis visto}} a este hombre que sube? Ciertamente sube para desafiar a Israel. Y al hombre que lo mate, el rey lo enriquecerá con grandes riquezas, y le dará su hija, y hará libre la casa de su padre en Israel».
es.B: Los hombres de Israel decían: «¿{{plural_you:Han visto|Habéis visto}} a ese hombre que sube? ¡Sube para desafiar a Israel! Al hombre que lo mate, el rey le dará grandes riquezas. También le dará a su hija, y librará de cargas a la familia de su padre en Israel».
es.R: Los soldados israelitas se decían unos a otros: «¿{{plural_you:Ven|Veis}} a este hombre? Sale una y otra vez para insultar a Israel. El rey hará muy rico al hombre que lo mate. También dejará que ese hombre se case con su hija, y la familia de su padre ya no tendrá que pagar impuestos ni trabajar para el rey».

fr.L: Et les hommes d’Israël dirent : « Avez-vous vu cet homme qui monte ? C’est pour défier Israël qu’il monte. Et l’homme qui le frappera, le roi l’enrichira de grandes richesses, et il lui donnera sa fille, et il rendra libre en Israël la maison de son père. »
fr.B: Les hommes d’Israël disaient : « Avez-vous vu cet homme qui s’avance ? C’est pour défier Israël qu’il s’avance ! Le roi donnera de grandes richesses à celui qui le tuera. Il lui donnera aussi sa fille et rendra libre en Israël la famille de son père. »
fr.R: Les soldats israélites se disaient entre eux : « Vous voyez cet homme ? Il vient sans arrêt pour insulter Israël. Le roi rendra très riche celui qui le tuera. Il lui donnera aussi sa fille en mariage, et la famille de son père n’aura plus à payer d’impôts ni à travailler pour le roi. »

vi.L: Người Y-sơ-ra-ên nói: "Các anh có thấy người đang đi lên này không? Hắn đi lên chính là để thách thức Y-sơ-ra-ên. Người nào giết được hắn, vua sẽ làm cho người ấy giàu có với nhiều của cải, sẽ gả con gái mình cho người ấy, và sẽ cho nhà cha người ấy được tự do trong Y-sơ-ra-ên."
vi.B: Quân Y-sơ-ra-ên nói với nhau: "Các anh có thấy người đang tiến lên đó không? Hắn ra để thách thức Y-sơ-ra-ên! Ai giết được hắn, vua sẽ ban cho nhiều của cải. Vua cũng sẽ gả con gái mình cho người ấy, và cho gia đình cha người ấy được miễn mọi nghĩa vụ trong Y-sơ-ra-ên."
vi.R: Quân lính Y-sơ-ra-ên nói với nhau: "Các anh có thấy người này không? Hắn cứ ra đây sỉ nhục Y-sơ-ra-ên. Ai giết được hắn, vua sẽ làm cho người ấy rất giàu. Vua cũng sẽ gả con gái mình cho người ấy, và gia đình cha người ấy sẽ không phải nộp thuế hay làm việc cho vua nữa."

decisions.choice: the rewards: wealth, the king's daughter, freedom for the family
decisions.reason: The king promises riches, marriage into the royal family (18:17-27) and that the winner's family will be "free". This probably means free from the taxes and forced labor a king could demand (8:11-17).

decisions.choice: surely he comes up to defy Israel
decisions.reason: The small word at the start of the clause stresses it: this man comes up for no other purpose than to taunt Israel.

decisions.choice: will not have to pay taxes or work for the king anymore
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what "free" probably means. The exact privileges are not listed in the text.

decisions.choice: were saying to one another
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the soldiers were talking among themselves, as verse 26 shows.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֗ד אֶֽל־הָאֲנָשִׁ֞ים הָעֹמְדִ֣ים עִמּוֹ֮ לֵאמֹר֒ מַה־יֵּעָשֶׂ֗ה לָאִישׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר יַכֶּה֙ אֶת־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֣י הַלָּ֔ז וְהֵסִ֥יר חֶרְפָּ֖ה מֵעַ֣ל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּ֣י מִ֗י הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֤י הֶֽעָרֵל֙ הַזֶּ֔ה כִּ֣י חֵרֵ֔ף מַעַרְכ֖וֹת אֱלֹהִ֥ים חַיִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And said David to the men standing with him, saying, What will be done for the man who strikes down this Philistine and removes reproach from upon Israel? For who [is] this uncircumcised Philistine that he has defied [the] ranks of [the] living God?

en.L: And David said to the men who were standing with him, "What will be done for the man who strikes down this Philistine and takes away the disgrace from Israel? For who [is] this uncircumcised Philistine, that he has defied the ranks of the living God?"
en.B: David asked the men standing near him, "What will be done for whoever kills this Philistine and removes the disgrace from Israel? This uncircumcised Philistine, who is he, that he dares to defy the ranks of the living God?"
en.R: David asked the men standing near him, "What will the king do for the man who kills this Philistine and takes away Israel's shame? This Philistine is outside God's covenant. Who does he think he is, insulting the army of the living God?"

es.L: Y dijo David a los hombres que estaban con él: «¿Qué se hará al hombre que mate a este filisteo y quite la afrenta de sobre Israel? Porque ¿quién [es] este filisteo incircunciso para que desafíe las filas del Dios viviente?».
es.B: David preguntó a los hombres que estaban cerca de él: «¿Qué se hará por quien mate a este filisteo y quite la deshonra de Israel? Este filisteo incircunciso, ¿quién es él para atreverse a desafiar a las filas del Dios viviente?».
es.R: David preguntó a los hombres que estaban cerca de él: «¿Qué hará el rey por el hombre que mate a este filisteo y quite la vergüenza de Israel? Este filisteo está fuera del pacto de Dios. ¿Quién se cree que es para insultar al ejército del Dios viviente?».

fr.L: Et David dit aux hommes qui se tenaient avec lui : « Que fera-t-on pour l’homme qui frappera ce Philistin et qui ôtera l’opprobre de dessus Israël ? Car qui [est] ce Philistin, cet incirconcis, pour qu’il défie les rangs du Dieu vivant ? »
fr.B: David demanda aux hommes qui se tenaient près de lui : « Que fera-t-on pour celui qui tuera ce Philistin et ôtera la honte qui pèse sur Israël ? Qui est-il donc, ce Philistin incirconcis, pour oser défier les rangs du Dieu vivant ? »
fr.R: David a demandé aux hommes qui étaient près de lui : « Qu’est-ce que le roi fera pour l’homme qui tuera ce Philistin et qui enlèvera la honte d’Israël ? Ce Philistin ne fait pas partie de l’alliance de Dieu. Pour qui se prend-il, pour insulter l’armée du Dieu vivant ? »

vi.L: Đa-vít nói với những người đang đứng cạnh mình: "Người nào giết được người Phi-li-tin này và cất bỏ sự sỉ nhục khỏi Y-sơ-ra-ên thì sẽ được gì? Vì người Phi-li-tin không chịu cắt bì này [là] ai mà dám thách thức các hàng quân của Đức Chúa Trời hằng sống?"
vi.B: Đa-vít hỏi những người đứng gần mình: "Người nào giết tên Phi-li-tin này và cất đi sự sỉ nhục khỏi Y-sơ-ra-ên thì sẽ được gì? Tên Phi-li-tin không chịu cắt bì này là ai mà dám thách thức các hàng quân của Đức Chúa Trời hằng sống?"
vi.R: Đa-vít hỏi những người đứng gần mình: "Vua sẽ làm gì cho người giết tên Phi-li-tin này và cất đi nỗi nhục của Y-sơ-ra-ên? Tên Phi-li-tin này không thuộc về giao ước của Đức Chúa Trời. Hắn nghĩ hắn là ai mà dám sỉ nhục quân đội của Đức Chúa Trời hằng sống?"

decisions.choice: reproach: disgrace
decisions.reason: The noun comes from the verb "defy" in verse 10. As long as no one answers Goliath's taunt, Israel stands disgraced.

decisions.choice: uncircumcised: outside God's covenant
decisions.reason: Circumcision was the sign of God's covenant with Abraham's descendants (Genesis 17:10-14). Israel called the Philistines "the uncircumcised" as people outside that covenant (14:6; 31:4; Judges 14:3).

decisions.choice: the living God
decisions.reason: Israel's God is alive and acts, unlike the gods of the nations (Deuteronomy 5:26; Joshua 3:10). David sees that Goliath's taunt is aimed at God, whose army Israel is.

decisions.choice: is outside God's covenant
decisions.reason: Readable explains what "uncircumcised" means here, in the wording used for it throughout the book (14:6; 31:4).

decisions.choice: the king
decisions.reason: Readable names who will reward the winner, from verse 25.

decisions.choice: incirconcis
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note sets; Readable explains it, "ne fait pas partie de l'alliance de Dieu", as the English does (r-en-1).

decisions.choice: incircunciso
decisions.reason: The Samuel terms note's word for the Philistines' uncircumcision; Readable explains it as being outside God's covenant (m2), as the English does (r-en-1). Recorded once for this block.

decisions.choice: "không chịu cắt bì" (L, B); "không thuộc về giao ước của Đức Chúa Trời" (R)
decisions.reason: The Samuel terms note's word; Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "tên Phi-li-tin" in David's mouth
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "tên" before a person carries David's scorn for the man who defies God; the narrator keeps "người Phi-li-tin".

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ הָעָ֔ם כַּדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר כֹּ֣ה יֵעָשֶׂ֔ה לָאִ֖ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַכֶּֽנּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to him the people according to this word, saying, Thus will be done for the man who strikes him down.

en.L: And the people spoke to him according to this word, saying, "So it will be done for the man who strikes him down."
en.B: The troops repeated to him what they had said: "This is what will be done for the man who kills him."
en.R: The soldiers told him the same thing again: "That is what the king will do for the man who kills him."

es.L: Y el pueblo le habló conforme a esta palabra, diciendo: «Así se hará al hombre que lo mate».
es.B: La tropa le repitió lo que habían dicho: «Esto es lo que se hará por el hombre que lo mate».
es.R: Los soldados le volvieron a decir lo mismo: «Eso es lo que el rey hará por el hombre que lo mate».

fr.L: Et le peuple lui parla selon cette parole, disant : « Ainsi sera-t-il fait à l’homme qui le frappera. »
fr.B: Les soldats lui répétèrent ce qu’ils avaient dit : « Voilà ce qu’on fera pour celui qui le tuera. »
fr.R: Les soldats lui ont redit la même chose : « Voilà ce que le roi fera pour l’homme qui le tuera. »

vi.L: Dân chúng nói với cậu theo lời ấy rằng: "Người nào giết được hắn sẽ được như vậy."
vi.B: Quân lính nhắc lại cho cậu những gì họ đã nói: "Người nào giết được hắn sẽ được như vậy."
vi.R: Quân lính lại nói với cậu y như trước: "Đó là điều vua sẽ làm cho người giết được hắn."

decisions.choice: according to this word: the same words as verse 25
decisions.reason: The soldiers repeat the promises of verse 25.

decisions.choice: the king
decisions.reason: Readable names who will do it, as in verse 26.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע אֱלִיאָב֙ אָחִ֣יו הַגָּד֔וֹל בְּדַבְּר֖וֹ אֶל־הָאֲנָשִׁ֑ים וַיִּֽחַר־אַף֩ אֱלִיאָ֨ב בְּדָוִ֜ד וַיֹּ֣אמֶר׀לָמָּה־זֶּ֣ה יָרַ֗דְתָּ וְעַל־מִ֨י נָטַ֜שְׁתָּ מְעַ֨ט הַצֹּ֤אן הָהֵ֨נָּה֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר אֲנִ֧י יָדַ֣עְתִּי אֶת־זְדֹנְךָ֗ וְאֵת֙ רֹ֣עַ לְבָבֶ֔ךָ כִּ֗י לְמַ֛עַן רְא֥וֹת הַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה יָרָֽדְתָּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And heard Eliab his oldest brother when he spoke to the men, and burned [the] anger of Eliab against David, and he said, Why [is] this [that] you have come down? And with whom have you left those few sheep in the wilderness? I know your presumption and the evil of your heart, for to see the battle you have come down.

en.L: And Eliab his oldest brother heard when he spoke to the men, and Eliab's anger burned against David, and he said, "Why have you come down? And with whom did you leave those few sheep in the wilderness? I know your presumption and the evil of your heart, for you have come down to see the battle."
en.B: When Eliab, his oldest brother, heard him talking to the men, he grew angry with David and said, "Why have you come down here? Who did you leave those few sheep with out in the wilderness? I know your arrogance and the wickedness in your heart. You have come down for nothing but to see the fighting!"
en.R: David's oldest brother Eliab heard him talking with the men, and he became angry with David. He said, "Why did you come here? Who is taking care of those few sheep out in the wilderness? I know how proud you are and how bad your motives are. You only came to watch the fighting!"

es.L: Y lo oyó Eliab su hermano mayor cuando hablaba con los hombres, y se encendió la ira de Eliab contra David, y dijo: «¿Para qué has bajado? ¿Y con quién dejaste aquellas pocas ovejas en el desierto? Yo conozco tu soberbia y la maldad de tu corazón, porque para ver la batalla has bajado».
es.B: Cuando Eliab, su hermano mayor, lo oyó hablar con los hombres, se enojó con David y le dijo: «¿Para qué has bajado aquí? ¿Con quién dejaste esas pocas ovejas en el desierto? Conozco tu arrogancia y la maldad de tu corazón. ¡Solo has bajado para ver la pelea!».
es.R: Eliab, el hermano mayor de David, lo oyó hablar con los hombres y se enojó con él. Le dijo: «¿Para qué viniste? ¿Quién está cuidando esas pocas ovejas en el desierto? Yo sé lo orgulloso que eres y las malas intenciones que tienes. ¡Solo viniste a mirar la pelea!».

fr.L: Et Éliab, son frère aîné, l’entendit parler aux hommes, et la colère d’Éliab s’enflamma contre David, et il dit : « Pourquoi donc es-tu descendu ? Et à qui as-tu laissé ce peu de brebis dans le désert ? Moi, je connais ton insolence et la méchanceté de ton cœur, car c’est pour voir la bataille que tu es descendu. »
fr.B: Éliab, son frère aîné, l’entendit parler avec les hommes et se mit en colère contre David. Il lui dit : « Pourquoi es-tu descendu jusqu’ici ? À qui as-tu laissé tes quelques moutons, là-bas dans le désert ? Je connais ton orgueil et la méchanceté de ton cœur. Tu n’es descendu que pour voir la bataille ! »
fr.R: Éliab, le frère aîné de David, l’a entendu parler avec les hommes, et il s’est mis en colère contre David. Il lui a dit : « Pourquoi est-ce que tu es venu ici ? Qui s’occupe de tes quelques moutons, là-bas dans le désert ? Je sais combien tu es orgueilleux, et je connais tes mauvaises intentions. Tu es seulement venu pour regarder la bataille ! »

vi.L: Ê-li-áp, anh cả của cậu, nghe khi cậu nói với những người ấy, thì cơn giận của Ê-li-áp nổi lên với Đa-vít, và anh nói: "Sao em xuống đây? Em để mấy con chiên ít ỏi kia trong hoang mạc cho ai? Anh biết tính tự phụ và lòng gian ác của em; vì em xuống đây là để xem đánh trận."
vi.B: Khi Ê-li-áp, anh cả của cậu, nghe cậu nói chuyện với những người ấy, anh nổi giận với Đa-vít và nói: "Sao em xuống đây? Mấy con chiên ít ỏi ngoài hoang mạc kia em bỏ cho ai trông? Anh biết tính kiêu căng và lòng gian xảo của em. Em xuống đây chỉ để xem đánh nhau thôi!"
vi.R: Ê-li-áp, anh cả của Đa-vít, nghe cậu nói chuyện với những người kia thì nổi giận với cậu. Anh nói: "Sao em đến đây? Ai trông mấy con chiên ít ỏi ngoài hoang mạc kia? Anh biết em kiêu ngạo và có ý xấu thế nào rồi. Em chỉ đến để xem đánh nhau thôi!"

decisions.choice: presumption: pride that reaches above one's place
decisions.reason: The word means arrogance or insolence, thinking oneself more than one is. Eliab thinks his young brother is meddling in the business of soldiers.

decisions.choice: the evil of your heart
decisions.reason: Eliab claims to know David's heart. But Yahweh, who looks at the heart, had passed over Eliab and chosen David (16:7).

decisions.choice: those few sheep: scorn for David's work
decisions.reason: Eliab makes David's flock sound small and his job unimportant, and blames him for leaving it.

decisions.choice: how bad your motives are
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of "the evil of your heart": Eliab says David came for a wrong reason.

decisions.choice: Eliab says "anh" for himself and "em" to David; David answers in the same pair
decisions.reason: As the Genesis terms note for brothers; Eliab's anger shows in his words, and "mày" would be cruder than the Hebrew.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֔ד מֶ֥ה עָשִׂ֖יתִי עָ֑תָּה הֲל֖וֹא דָּבָ֥ר הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And said David, What have I done now? [Was] it not [only] a word?

en.L: And David said, "What have I done now? [Was] it not [only] a word?"
en.B: David said, "What have I done now? Can I not even ask a question?"
en.R: David answered, "What have I done wrong now? I was only asking a question."

es.L: Y dijo David: «¿Qué he hecho ahora? ¿No [era] [solo] una palabra?».
es.B: David dijo: «¿Y ahora qué he hecho? ¿Ni siquiera puedo hacer una pregunta?».
es.R: David contestó: «¿Qué hice de malo ahora? Solo estaba haciendo una pregunta».

fr.L: Et David dit : « Qu’ai-je fait maintenant ? N’[était]-ce pas [seulement] une parole ? »
fr.B: David répondit : « Qu’est-ce que j’ai encore fait ? Je ne peux même pas poser une question ? »
fr.R: David a répondu : « Qu’est-ce que j’ai encore fait de mal ? Je posais seulement une question. »

vi.L: Đa-vít nói: "Bây giờ em đã làm gì? Chẳng phải [chỉ là] một lời thôi sao?"
vi.B: Đa-vít nói: "Em lại làm gì nữa đây? Hỏi một câu cũng không được sao?"
vi.R: Đa-vít đáp: "Em lại làm gì sai nữa? Em chỉ hỏi một câu thôi mà."

decisions.choice: was it not only a word?: David was just asking
decisions.reason: The words mean "It was only talk": David says he has only asked a question. The word for "word" can also mean "matter" or "reason", so the clause has also been read "Is there not a reason?", that is, a good cause to speak.

decisions.choice: now: once again
decisions.reason: "Now" suggests that Eliab has found fault with David before.

decisions.choice: I was only asking a question
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into the statement it implies.

source.text: וַיִּסֹּ֤ב מֵֽאֶצְלוֹ֙ אֶל־מ֣וּל אַחֵ֔ר וַיֹּ֖אמֶר כַּדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַיְשִׁבֻ֤הוּ הָעָם֙ דָּבָ֔ר כַּדָּבָ֖ר הָרִאשֽׁוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And he turned from beside him toward another, and said according to this word; and answered him the people word according to the former word.

en.L: And he turned away from him toward another and spoke according to this word; and the people answered him a word like the first word.
en.B: He turned away from him to someone else and asked the same thing, and the troops gave him the same answer as before.
en.R: Then David turned to someone else and asked the same question. And the people gave him the same answer.

es.L: Y se apartó de él hacia otro, y habló conforme a esta palabra; y el pueblo le respondió palabra conforme a la palabra primera.
es.B: Se apartó de él, se dirigió a otro y le preguntó lo mismo, y la tropa le dio la misma respuesta que antes.
es.R: Entonces David se volvió a otra persona y le hizo la misma pregunta. Y la gente le dio la misma respuesta.

fr.L: Et il se détourna de lui vers un autre et parla selon cette parole ; et le peuple lui répondit une parole comme la première parole.
fr.B: Il se détourna de lui pour s’adresser à quelqu’un d’autre et posa la même question, et les soldats lui firent la même réponse qu’avant.
fr.R: Alors David s’est tourné vers quelqu’un d’autre et il a posé la même question. Et les gens lui ont donné la même réponse.

vi.L: Cậu quay khỏi anh mình sang một người khác và nói theo lời ấy; dân chúng trả lời cậu một lời như lời trước.
vi.B: Cậu quay sang một người khác và hỏi cùng một câu ấy, và quân lính cũng trả lời cậu như trước.
vi.R: Rồi Đa-vít quay sang hỏi một người khác cùng câu hỏi đó. Và người ta cũng trả lời cậu y như trước.

decisions.choice: he turned toward another: David ignores Eliab
decisions.reason: David does not argue with his brother but keeps asking. His persistence is how his words reach Saul (verse 31).

source.text: וַיְּשָּֽׁמְעוּ֙הַדְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֣ר דָּוִ֑ד וַיַּגִּ֥דוּ לִפְנֵֽי־שָׁא֖וּל וַיִּקָּחֵֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And were heard the words which David spoke, and they told [them] before Saul, and he took him.

en.L: And the words that David spoke were heard, and they told [them] before Saul, and he sent for him.
en.B: What David said was overheard and reported to Saul, and Saul sent for him.
en.R: Some men heard what David was saying and told Saul about it. So Saul sent for David.

es.L: Y se oyeron las palabras que habló David, y [las] contaron delante de Saúl, y él lo hizo traer.
es.B: Alguien oyó lo que David decía y se lo contó a Saúl, y Saúl lo mandó llamar.
es.R: Algunos hombres oyeron lo que David decía y se lo contaron a Saúl. Entonces Saúl mandó a buscar a David.

fr.L: Et les paroles que David avait dites furent entendues, et on [les] rapporta devant Saül, et il le fit venir.
fr.B: Les propos de David furent entendus et rapportés à Saül, qui le fit appeler.
fr.R: Des hommes ont entendu ce que David disait et ils l’ont raconté à Saül. Alors Saül a fait venir David.

vi.L: Những lời Đa-vít nói có người nghe được, và họ thuật lại trước mặt Sau-lơ, và ông cho đem cậu đến.
vi.B: Những lời Đa-vít nói có người nghe được và đem tâu với Sau-lơ, và Sau-lơ cho gọi cậu đến.
vi.R: Có mấy người nghe những gì Đa-vít nói và kể lại cho Sau-lơ. Vậy Sau-lơ cho gọi Đa-vít đến.

decisions.choice: he took him: Saul had him brought
decisions.reason: The verb "take" here means that Saul summoned David and had him brought to him.

decisions.choice: Some men
decisions.reason: Readable supplies a subject for the passive "were heard".

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִד֙ אֶל־שָׁא֔וּל אַל־יִפֹּ֥ל לֵב־אָדָ֖ם עָלָ֑יו עַבְדְּךָ֣ יֵלֵ֔ךְ וְנִלְחַ֖ם עִם־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֥י הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said David to Saul, Let not fall [the] heart of a man on account of him; your servant will go and fight with this Philistine.

en.L: And David said to Saul, "Let no man's heart fall because of him; your servant will go and fight with this Philistine."
en.B: David said to Saul, "No one should lose heart because of this man! Your servant will go and fight this Philistine."
en.R: David said to Saul, "Nobody should be afraid because of this Philistine. I will go and fight him myself!"

es.L: Y dijo David a Saúl: «Que no decaiga el corazón de nadie a causa de él; tu siervo irá y peleará con este filisteo».
es.B: David le dijo a Saúl: «¡Que nadie se desanime por causa de ese hombre! Tu siervo irá a pelear contra este filisteo».
es.R: David le dijo a Saúl: «Nadie debe tener miedo por causa de este filisteo. ¡Yo mismo iré a pelear contra él!».

decisions.choice: let no man's heart fall: let no one lose courage
decisions.reason: For the heart to fall is to lose courage. David speaks to the fear of verses 11 and 24.

decisions.choice: no man's heart
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation reads "let not my lord's heart fall", so that David speaks to Saul's own fear. The received Hebrew text says "no man's heart". This is given from general knowledge; reviewers must check it against a critical edition.

decisions.choice: your servant: a polite way of saying "I"
decisions.reason: Speaking to the king, David calls himself "your servant" (also verses 34 and 36). It is the courtesy of a subject, not a statement that he is a slave.

decisions.choice: I
decisions.reason: Readable uses "I" for the polite "your servant" here and in verses 34 and 36.

decisions.choice: ton serviteur (L, B); moi, je (R)
decisions.reason: David's polite "your servant" before the king (m3) is "ton serviteur" at Literal and Balanced, as the Samuel terms note sets; Readable says "je", as the English (r-en-1), here and in verses 34 and 36.

decisions.choice: tu siervo (L, B); yo (R)
decisions.reason: “Your servant” is a polite way of saying “I” before the king (m3). As the terms note sets, Literal and Balanced keep “tu siervo”; Readable says “yo”, as the English Readable says “I” (r-en-1).

decisions.choice: "đầy tớ của vua" (L), "đầy tớ của bệ hạ" (B), "tôi" (R) for "your servant"
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note for a subject speaking to the king; the Balanced title "bệ hạ" stands in the phrase too.

en.B: Saul answered David, "You cannot go out against this Philistine and fight him. You are a mere youth, and he has been trained for war since his own youth."
en.R: Saul said, "You cannot fight this Philistine. You are just a young man, and he has been a soldier all his life."

es.R: Saúl le dijo: «Tú no puedes pelear con este filisteo. Eres apenas un joven, y él ha sido soldado toda su vida».

fr.L: Et Saül dit à David : « Tu ne peux pas aller contre ce Philistin pour combattre avec lui, car tu [es] un jeune garçon, et lui, [il est] un homme de guerre depuis sa jeunesse. »

fr.R: Saül a dit : « Tu ne peux pas te battre contre ce Philistin. Tu n’es qu’un jeune homme, et lui, il est soldat depuis toujours. »

vi.B: Sau-lơ đáp với Đa-vít: "Ngươi không thể ra đánh tên Phi-li-tin này được. Ngươi chỉ là một thiếu niên, còn hắn đã được luyện tập chiến trận từ khi còn trẻ."
vi.R: Sau-lơ nói: "Ngươi không thể đánh tên Phi-li-tin này được. Ngươi chỉ là một chàng trai trẻ, còn hắn đã làm lính suốt đời."

decisions.choice: a youth: a young man
decisions.reason: The word names a boy or young man, often one not yet a seasoned soldier. Saul uses it twice, of David now and of Goliath in his early years: the giant has been at war longer than David has been alive. The same word is used of David in verses 42, 55 and 58.

decisions.choice: a man of war: a trained warrior
decisions.reason: The phrase means a professional soldier (Joshua 17:1). Ironically, 16:18 had already called David "a man of war".

decisions.choice: came ... carried off: what happened from time to time
decisions.reason: The verbs here and in verse 35 describe what used to happen: whenever a wild animal took a sheep, David went after it. They could also tell of one occasion when both a lion and a bear came.

decisions.choice: your servant: as in verse 32
decisions.reason: David continues to speak of himself politely as "your servant".

decisions.choice: the lion and the bear: wild animals of the land
decisions.reason: Lions and bears lived in the hills and thickets of Israel at this time (Judges 14:5; 2 Kings 2:24). A shepherd was expected to defend the flock (Genesis 31:39; Amos 3:12).

decisions.choice: I
decisions.reason: As in verse 32.

decisions.choice: its beard: the hair of its chin, its jaw
decisions.reason: The word means beard or chin. Of a lion or bear it means the jaw or the hair under it, where David seized the animal.

decisions.reason: The clause states what happened if the animal attacked David instead of running.

decisions.choice: jaw
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "jaw", since "beard" sounds odd for a wild animal.

decisions.choice: imparfait ("je sortais", "je le frappais") at every level
decisions.reason: David tells what used to happen whenever a wild animal took a sheep (m1 of verse 34); French says repeated past action with the imparfait.

decisions.choice: for he has defied the ranks of the living God: David's reason for confidence
decisions.reason: David's courage does not rest on his skill but on the fact that Goliath has insulted the living God (verse 26). God's honor is at stake, so David expects God to act.

decisions.choice: the lion and the bear: such animals

decisions.choice: I; who is outside God's covenant

records.literal_gloss: And said David, Yahweh who delivered me from [the] hand of the lion and from [the] hand of the bear, he will deliver me from [the] hand of this Philistine. And said Saul to David, Go, and Yahweh will be with you.

en.L: And David said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, who delivered me from the hand of the lion and from the hand of the bear, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will deliver me from the hand of this Philistine." And Saul said to David, "Go, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will be with you."
en.B: David went on, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} rescued me from the power of the lion and of the bear, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rescue me from the power of this Philistine." Then Saul said to David, "Go. May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} be with you."
en.R: David said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} kept me safe from the lion and the bear, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will keep me safe from this Philistine too." Then Saul said to David, "Go, and may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} be with you."

es.R: David dijo: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me protegió del león y del oso, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} también me protegerá de este filisteo». Entonces Saúl le dijo a David: «Ve, y que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} esté contigo».
